title: Two showing requests want the same time
when: Two buyers ask for showings that overlap on the calendar.
steps: If one of them protects a deadline (for example a hot lead), it wins and you are offered the chance to move the other.
Otherwise the first one confirmed keeps the slot.
Agent 06 (Showing Scheduler) does not book the second; it asks you about the calendar conflict.
never: Book both and hope it works out.
why: A double-booked showing leaves a buyer waiting on a doorstep and an occupant disturbed twice.
you_see: A question about the calendar conflict for the second buyer.
test: Buyer B1 asks for 10:00 and buyer B2 for 10:15 at the same listing. B1 is confirmed; B2 goes to you. No alternative time is worked out for B2 today (stated in the agent's DECISIONS.md). The protected-deadline case is played in a separate scene (scene 8, showing bump).

title: The person asking for a showing cannot be identified
when: Someone asks for a showing, which means access to a home, and their identity has not been verified.
steps: Agent 06 cancels the showing; it is never confirmed.
The cancellation and the reason (identity not verified) are written in the client's history.
never: Give access to a home to someone whose identity is not verified. No exceptions.
why: Showings put strangers inside people's homes. Unverified access is a safety and liability risk.
you_see: The cancelled showing in the client's history, with the reason.
test: Buyer B1 has a buyer agreement on file but no verified identity, and asks for a 10:00 showing.

title: Someone asks to "just let them in"
when: A message asks for someone to be let into a property without a scheduled, verified showing.
steps: Agent 11 (Client Communication) catches the request and raises a legal-line alert for you.
Nobody is let in; no access is arranged.
never: Arrange access outside the showing process.
why: Access to a home is the line. Letting someone in on a message is how break-ins and liability start.
you_see: A legal-line alert quoting the request.
test: A client writes: "We're running late, can you just let them in to the house?"

title: Someone does not show up for a showing
when: A showing is reported as a no-show.
steps: Agent 06 records the no-show.
It asks Agent 11 to send a feedback request in a neutral tone, with no reproach.
never: Send a scolding or blaming message about the no-show.
why: People miss appointments for many reasons. A neutral note keeps the relationship and still gets the facts.
you_see: The no-show in the client's history; a neutral feedback request sent.
test: Buyer B1 has a confirmed 10:00 showing, then writes "The other agent never showed up".

title: A same-day showing is asked for at an occupied home
when: A buyer asks for a showing at an occupied home with less notice than the minimum.
steps: Agent 06 reads occupancy from the listing record.
The notice rule still applies (24 hours in your settings), same day or not.
Nothing is booked; the buyer is offered the first time that meets the notice rule.
never: Squeeze in a showing at an occupied home without the required notice.
why: Occupants are entitled to notice. Short-notice showings breed seller complaints.
you_see: A message to the buyer offering the first allowed time.
test: The listing record says occupied. At 10:00 a buyer asks for 15:00 the same day (5 hours' notice against 24).

title: Someone asks for a lockbox code or access code in a message
when: A message asks for a lockbox combination or an access code.
steps: Agent 11 catches the request and raises a legal-line alert for you.
The code is never sent in a message; access goes only through the access-custody process.
never: Send an access code or lockbox combination in any message.
why: A code in a message can be forwarded to anyone. Access stays in the custody process.
you_see: A legal-line alert quoting the request.
test: A client writes: "What's the lockbox combo for the house on Elm?"

title: A showing is asked for inside an occupied home's notice window
when: A buyer asks for a time that is too soon under the notice rule for an occupied home.
steps: If the listing record does not say whether the home is occupied, Agent 06 treats it as occupied.
Nothing is booked; the buyer is offered the first time that meets the notice rule.
Nobody is asked to waive the notice.
never: Ask the seller to waive notice unprompted.
why: Pressure on a seller to give up their notice protection is a complaint waiting to happen. If they want to waive it, that is their call.
you_see: A message to the buyer offering the first allowed time.
test: The listing record says nothing about occupancy. A buyer asks at noon for 08:00 the next day (20 hours against 24).

title: The same showing agent no-shows twice
when: A showing agent has failed to show up twice.
steps: Before confirming a third showing with that agent, Agent 06 flags the pattern to you.
never: Keep booking an agent who keeps not showing up, without telling you.
why: Repeated no-shows waste sellers' time and your reputation with them.
you_see: A flag naming the pattern before the third confirmation.

title: A buyer asks for two showings too close together
when: One buyer asks for two showings that fall within the buffer time between appointments.
steps: Agent 06 confirms the first.
It does not book the second; it asks you about the conflict (inside the 30-minute buffer).
never: Double-book and hope the buyer gets there in time.
why: Travel and overruns are real. A late buyer means a waiting occupant and a bad first impression.
you_see: A question about the calendar conflict within the 30-minute buffer.
test: Buyer B1 asks for one listing at 10:00 and another at 10:20 the same day.

title: A feedback request goes unanswered
when: Feedback was asked for after a showing and nobody answers.
steps: Agent 06 asks for feedback through Agent 11 on the daily run after the showing.
After two asks with no answer, it stops and records that the cap was reached.
why: Nagging the people who show your listings burns goodwill with the agent network.
you_see: At most two feedback requests per showing.
test: A showing on October 17. The daily clock runs every day from the 16th to the 20th. Exactly two feedback requests go out, then the cap stops them.

title: A showing is asked for at a property under contract
when: A buyer asks to see a property whose listing record says it is under contract (pending).
steps: Agent 06 checks the listing's current status with Agent 05 (MLS & Listing Management) first.
The status is not one that allows showings, so nothing is booked.
It asks you, naming the status.
never: Assume a listing is active and book the showing.
why: Showing a property under contract can interfere with the deal and mislead the buyer.
you_see: A question saying the property status "pending" does not allow showings.
test: A listing goes live and then pending with a signed contract. A buyer asks to see it.

title: The weekly seller report is due
when: The weekday you signed for seller reports arrives.
steps: For each listing in your setting, Agent 06 counts the week's showings and feedback.
It holds the report and asks you: continue sends it to the seller through Agent 11; cancel skips this week.
It holds only one report per listing per week, however many times the daily run happens.
Agent 11 sends to the seller only with the seller's consent on record; without it, it tells you to record the consent.
never: Send a seller report you have not seen, or send two in one week.
why: The seller report speaks for you to your client. You see it before it goes.
you_see: A held report with its counts, asking you to continue or cancel.
test: You sign Monday reports for listing SYN-L001 (seller S1), and the seller's consent is on record. One showing happens. On Monday the report is held (1 showing, 0 with feedback); you continue and it is sent to the seller once; the daily run on the same day does not hold a second one.

title: The seller report setting is wrong
when: A signed seller report setting cannot be read (for example the weekday "funday").
steps: Agent 06 rejects the whole setting; nothing changes.
It tells you the setting was rejected.
never: Apply part of a broken setting, or guess what it meant.
why: A half-applied setting gives reports on the wrong day or for the wrong listings.
you_see: A question saying the seller report setting was rejected.
test: A signed seller report setting with the weekday "funday".
